records.Concise description: An open-source DIY Bitcoin and Lightning node distribution centered on Raspberry Pi and operator education.
records.Deeper researched summary: RaspiBlitz combines a Bitcoin full node with LND and/or Core Lightning plus a menu-driven environment for installing operator tools such as RTL, BTC RPC Explorer, Electrum servers, BTCPay Server, and other services. It is a node stack and orchestration project rather than an independent Bitcoin or Lightning protocol implementation. Its explicit educational and DIY orientation makes it distinct from more general home-server platforms.
records.Launch / history: RaspiBlitz has been developed since the late 2010s as a home-built Bitcoin/Lightning node project and continues to publish maintained documentation and version updates.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It became one of the best-known pathways for individuals to learn full-node and Lightning operations on commodity hardware.
records.Verification basis: Current official docs and repository/change-log evidence establish ongoing node-stack maintenance.
Research notes / uncertainties: RaspiBlitz bundles upstream node implementations; do not attribute their consensus rules or Lightning protocol behavior to RaspiBlitz itself.
Bundled app versions change frequently; reverify before publishing version-specific claims.

records.Concise description: A browser-managed Bitcoin and Lightning node platform that integrates full-node, Electrum, explorer, Lightning, and related self-hosted applications.
records.Deeper researched summary: myNode packages upstream open-source Bitcoin and Lightning software behind a local web management interface and offers both community software and commercial hardware/premium options. Current documentation lists Bitcoin full-node, Lightning, Electrum Server, mempool, BTCPay, RTL, and many other apps. The canonical repository had same-day development activity on August 15, 2026, establishing a clearly active lifecycle.
records.Launch / history: myNode was created in 2019 as an easier personal-node stack and continues active hardware/software and open-source development through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a durable personal-node distribution that makes multiple Network and Payments components easier to operate together without becoming a new Bitcoin implementation itself.
records.Verification basis: Current first-party site/docs and GitHub metadata showed active repository pushes on 2026-08-15.
Research notes / uncertainties: myNode bundles upstream software; do not credit it with upstream consensus or Lightning protocol semantics.
Wallet/custody properties depend on the specific application and configuration.

records.Concise description: An open-source web interface for operating LND, Core Lightning, and Eclair nodes, including channels, payments, liquidity tools, and node analytics.
records.Deeper researched summary: RTL requires an existing functioning Lightning node and provides a management layer over that node's API. It can control multiple nodes and supports major implementations including LND, Core Lightning, and Eclair. Features include payment/invoice operations, channel management, reports, authentication options, and integrations such as swaps. That makes RTL canonically node-management infrastructure rather than a standalone wallet, preserving the deliberate WALLETS exclusion decision.
records.Launch / history: RTL launched in 2018. The canonical repository was pushed on August 12, 2026, and the project site describes ongoing community-supported operation.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the most established implementation-agnostic Lightning node-management interfaces and an important operational layer between node daemons and human operators.
records.Verification basis: First-party site and GitHub metadata establish the node-management scope, multi-implementation support, 2018 launch, and active August 2026 maintenance.
Research notes / uncertainties: RTL is not a Lightning implementation and does not operate without a backend node.
Payment functions in the UI do not make RTL canonically a wallet; spending authority resides in the connected node/configuration.
Experimental feature labels on the site may lag current implementation status; reverify before feature-specific copy.

records.Concise description: An open-source LND-focused dashboard and automation system for analyzing node data, rebalancing, fee management, and routine operator tasks.
records.Deeper researched summary: LNDg connects to an existing LND node and turns node/channel data into dashboards and operational automation. Its canonical repository describes a lightweight GUI that analyzes LND data and uses a backend database for maintenance tools such as rebalancing. It is implementation-specific to LND rather than a general Lightning wallet. Active repository pushes through July 26, 2026 support inclusion in NETWORK after WALLETS deliberately deferred it here.
records.Launch / history: LNDg began in 2021 and remains actively maintained, with canonical repository pushes in July 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It represents the analytics/automation side of Lightning node operations and shows how operator policy can be layered above the underlying LND implementation.
records.Verification basis: Canonical repository description and active July 2026 pushes establish current lifecycle and node-management scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: LNDg requires LND; it is not a Lightning protocol implementation.
Automation settings can materially affect fees, liquidity, and routing behavior; do not present defaults as protocol rules.
